Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short trial respite + conversion mechanics

Hi Irene,

First, thanks for all the support this week — the Redwood runtime made our prototype inference significantly more predictable which the data team loved. We're almost through our integration checklist but ran into two blockers: a spike in request volume consumed our remaining credits, and the compliance team needs one more log export to finish a SOC review.

Can we get a short 10–14 day extension on the current timeboxed POC so we can finish the audit and run a final accuracy sweep? Also, if Lumenox commits to a 6-month pilot after the extension, what's the best way to structure a conversion discount on the first month / committed tokens? We'd prefer a simple path (no complex credits buckets) — something our procurement team can sign off quickly.

Attaching a brief usage snapshot (we'll send the log export separately).

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
Head of ML Platforms
Lumenox Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short trial respite + conversion mechanics

Hi Tom — really glad the runtime improvements helped. Short answer: yes, we can help and we have two pragmatic paths depending on how fast procurement moves.

Option A — Short free respite + streamlined conversion (lowest friction):
- 7 days complimentary extension on the existing POC window (no extra invoicing).
- If Lumenox signs a 6-month committed pilot within 30 days of the extension end date, Redwood will apply a 15% discount on the first invoice (applies to committed tokens for month 1).
- We include a one-off engineering credit (2 support days) to help with the SOC log export.

Option B — 14 days extension + simple prepaid credit (if procurement wants an invoiceable item):
- 14 days extension funded by a small prepay (50% credit of an estimated month) that offsets the first invoice; refundable against committed usage if you convert to a 6-month pilot.
- If converted, we ladder a 10% discount on month 1 instead of the 15% concession above.

I'll loop in finance and Ben (pricing lead) for approval on the formal amendment language — small legal/finance tweaks will be needed for the refundable prepay flow. If you want the fastest path for procurement, Option A tends to close quicker.

I attached a short POC amendment template you can share with procurement; we'll keep the wording lightweight.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachment: POC-Amendment-v1.pdf (PDF, 18 KB)
